title: Anyon ladder: generic $q$ ↔ root-of-unity ↔ $q \to 1$
html:
Remark. Anyon ladder: generic q ↔ root-of-unity ↔ q \to 1

Remark (anyon ladder under the observation functor). The three preceding conjectures organize into a single ladder indexed by the deformation parameter q:

q regime Substrate state Observation image
Generic q Abelian anyons in H_n(R, q) Topological braiding matrices
q = e^{2\pi i / k} Non-abelian anyons in \mathrm{MTC}_k Finite fusion / F- and R-matrices
q \to 1 Symmetric-group representations Pauli (\pm 1) statistics

Reading the ladder downwards represents the observation functor \tau acting on a cooling substrate. Anyonic braiding loses information at each step, while the categorical algebraic substrate persists throughout. We use Kashiwara crystal traversals to compute pair production and stable masses. These map the fusion rules of the appropriate rung: the generic Hecke fluid for high-energy interactions, \mathrm{MTC}_k for topologically ordered phases, and \mathbb{Z}[S_n] for the classical-statistics regime accessed by macroscopic detectors.

Algorithmic synthesis. The reduction engine selects the rung by the value of q supplied to the substrate. It uses generic q for the open-ended Hecke evaluation, a root of unity for fusion-category enumeration, and q \to 1 for the Pauli/Bose decomposition. The same canonical-basis machinery applies at every rung. Only the specialization map changes.
